title: VPC deployment certification: smoke runbook, model-load attestations, and API readiness gating
creator: Amrita Shah
description: Create an executable certification runbook and automation harness that validates VPC/private deployments immediately after Terraform apply or rolling upgrades. The runbook must perform API readiness checks, model-load and KV cache warmup, golden-path smoke requests across representative personas, and output a deterministic pass/fail signature (health signature) that can be consumed by deploy pipelines and CD gates.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook executes as a single orchestrated job (k8s Job or ephemeral VM) after terraform apply and returns HTTP 200 within the pipeline for green path deployments.

Model-load stage validates that target model(s) can be instantiated in under 45s for 8-bit quantized variants and 90s for fp16 variants on Dedicated/private hardware; measured times are recorded and uploaded to the deployment artifact store.
KV cache sanity: pre-warm of KV cache with synthetic prefixes results in <5% tail latency increase for 1k token continuation compared to warmed baseline.

API readiness checks cover: TLS handshake, token-auth verification, route-level health (generate/chat/embeddings), streaming handshake, and model manifest hash verification (manifest_hash on deployed artifact matches expected value).

Smoke traffic uses three synthetic personas (chat-bot, summarizer, search-re-ranker) and must pass soft semantic checks (contains expected keywords) and hard checks (no runtime errors, response schema valid).
Health signature (JSON blob) is produced with fields: pass/fail, measured latencies, model_load_time, kv_warmup_status, manifest_hash, and artifact_url; CI consumes this blob and gates the rollout.
Automatic remediation hints are emitted on failure (e.g., suggest scaling, kernel rollback, or re-run with higher resource caps).
steps: Add terraform module hook: post_apply_hook triggers the certification job with environment metadata and expected manifest hash.
Provision ephemeral runner in customer VPC using private deploy credentials; runner pulls the model manifest and the runtime job bundle from artifacts.
Execute API readiness checks: TLS, auth, GET /v1/health, generate warmup call, streaming handshake.
Instantiate model(s) using the same runtime invocation as production and measure load time, memory, and peak GPU utilisation (via nvml).
Run KV cache warmup sequence (100 synthetic prefixes across 10 seeds) and measure token step latencies and hit rates.
Execute smoke persona scenarios (10 short chats, 20 summarizations, 50 embedding calls) and validate schema and keyword heuristics.
Aggregate results into the health signature, store to S3/artifact-store, and POST signature to the CD gating endpoint.
technotes: Use existing runtime image runtime-1.22-compatible with kernel-selection hooks; runtime picks quantized kernels when model manifest indicates q4_0 or q8_0.
Loader harness: use loader-bench v2 with deterministic RNG seed to ensure repeatable model-load timings.
Manifest hash verification: compute SHA256 of model artifact metadata and compare with expected value from deploy plan.
KV warmup uses our prefix-cache tool (kvcache-primer) which writes incremental KV entries and validates by replaying a continuation workload.
Health signature schema defined in confluence: /confluence/infra/vpc-health-signature-schema (link below).
